strategies.name: Cash-secured puts (ICICI 300PE, HDFC 840PE)
strategies.construction: Sell puts below market with full cash set aside for delivery
strategies.numbers: +33,000 ICICI and +28,000 HDFC in May 2020
strategies.best_regime: moderately bullish with stocks near support
strategies.adjustments: take delivery if assigned; roll if view changes
strategies.risks: sharp breakdown below strike forces delivery at loss

strategies.name: Put ratio spread (9100PE bought / 8500PE sold)
strategies.construction: Long lower put, short further-OTM puts
strategies.best_regime: mildly bearish to flat
strategies.adjustments: close short side on breakdown
strategies.risks: accelerated loss beyond short strikes

quotes: People lose money because they do not want to lose money - they expect zero-loss calls, which is impossible.

summary: Bank Nifty shot up ~2,400 points vindicating oversold call; Nifty expired 9,490; bear cases (China, GDP fear, zero auto sales, virus, border) systematically rebutted; FIIs turned buyers last 2 sessions; June target 10,000-10,200.
lessons: Markets worry about lead indicators (reopening), not lag indicators (GDP).
Known news (zero auto sales) is already priced - markets react only to surprises (efficient market hypothesis).
When FIIs turn buyers after a long selling streak, Nifty typically adds ~1,000 points.

summary: Q&A episode: expiry-day mechanics for hedged shorts (removing the long leg makes the short naked; index options cash-settle, stock options physically deliver if ITM - square off yourself); F&O ban-list illiquidity; advice to avoid stock F&O below ~1 crore capital and prefer indices; collateral eligibility (REC bonds, property, ELSS under 3 years ineligible); 50% cash margin component rule; Bharat Bond is cumulative, not annual-pay; option selling not advisable below ~10 lakh capital; no fixed timeline to become a successful trader.
lessons: Removing the protective long leg on expiry day converts your short into a naked position - margin and risk jump; close positions yourself rather than letting settlement decide.
Physical delivery applies only to stock F&O: short ITM call = give delivery, short ITM put = take delivery. Indices are cash-settled.
Collateral eligibility rule of thumb: anything not immediately liquidatable (property, REC/lock-in bonds, ELSS inside 3 years) cannot be pledged.
NSE margin rule: at least 50% of margin must be cash component - cash, FDs, liquid funds and Liquid BeES qualify; Bharat Bond counts as collateral, not cash.
quotes: Anything that cannot be liquidated immediately cannot be given as a collateral.

summary: Mechanics of the F&O ban (Market Wide Position Limit): MWPL = 20% of free-float market cap; a stock enters ban when combined open interest ends a day above 95% of MWPL; no fresh F&O positions next day (existing positions square-off only); ban lifts only when OI falls below 80%. Penalty for banned trading: 1% of contract value or 5,000 rupees, whichever is higher, capped at 1 lakh/day. Live examples: Vodafone Idea at 93.5% utilization, Canara Bank in ban at 88.5% (descending), Adani Enterprises at 88% not banned; nine stocks in ban for 12 August 2020.
lessons: MWPL math: 20% of free-float market cap caps total F&O open interest; speculative smallcaps hit it far sooner than large caps.
Ban asymmetry: entry at 95% utilization but exit only below 80% - ban lists persist for days and freeze hedgers mid-position.
During a ban you can only square off: no fresh futures or options positions, so adjustment trades become impossible exactly when risk peaks.
Trading a banned stock costs at least 5,000 rupees per lot (1% of contract value), capped at 1 lakh per day - plus unquantifiable exit-liquidity risk.
quotes: Usually the stocks that come under trading ban are the highly speculative stocks.

summary: Monthly account review: ~₹1.49 cr profit YTD on ~₹1 cr capital (~150%) despite September's Bank Nifty -20% series; September itself only ~₹10L. Breakdown: Bank Nifty -₹5.5L, offset by hedging (+₹1.5L), ratio spread (+₹1.18L), ITC call-selling cost reduction (avg → ~₹171), Nifty (+₹1.4L), SBI (+₹38K); Sensex options -₹2L on illiquidity, hedged via Nifty. Lifestyle/charity offered as the real P&L verification heuristic.
lessons: In a -20% Bank Nifty month, hedged leg income (+ ratio spreads) against directional losses is what keeps the year at 150%.
Illiquid instruments (Sensex options then) force you to hedge in a liquid proxy (Nifty) - liquidity is a position-sizing input.
Aggressive call selling against a falling stock positions cuts cost basis faster than averaging alone (ITC to ~171).
Judge any claimed P&L by capital trajectory and lifestyle/charity over time - screenshots prove nothing.

strategies.name: Hedged monthly book through expiry stress
strategies.construction: Directional futures/option legs + offsetting call hedges + occasional ratio spreads
strategies.numbers: Sep: BN -5.5L, hedges +1.5L, ratio +1.18L, ITC hedging +2.23L, Nifty +1.4L, SBI +38K, Sensex -2L → ~+10L on ~₹1 cr capital
strategies.best_regime: Volatile series where directional legs bleed
strategies.adjustments: Hedge in the next series when current-series data ends; move hedges to liquid proxies
strategies.risks: Illiquidity in new instruments (Sensex options) causes slippage and forced proxy hedging

quotes: Show me your one-year P&L - then look at the lifestyle and the charity, and you will know the truth.

summary: Nifty hits fresh all-time high; debunks MSCI-rebalancing explanation (global peers rallied more), credits global liquidity (DXY<91), vaccine hope; heavyweight recovery thesis; FII/DII flows and option-chain OI read; sold puts into the rally.
lessons: Ride the trend: as long as the rally is on, stay with it - do not predict its end.
Judge rallies by global breadth, not a single excuse like index rebalancing.
Heavyweight lag (Reliance/HDFC ~25% of Nifty) hiding strength signals upside when they catch up.
Max-OI put addition below price = firm bull grip; call unwinding confirms.
quotes: A bull market is born out of pessimism, grows out of skepticism, matures out of optimism and dies out of euphoria.
So as long as the rally is there, we ride the rally - that should be a trader's mentality.

summary: Live firefighting case study: a short Bajaj Finance/Finserv future plus sold call went against the position as the stock jumped 5% (4,900 to 5,150). Rescue: laddered put sales (4,500/4,700/4,800/4,900/5,000/5,200 strikes), added long January future, sold 5,500 call; ~1 crore additional margin deployed; position closed +1.49 lakh. Plus market-order pattern and VIX-decay outlook.
lessons: Firefighting works only with reserve capital: this rescue needed roughly 1 crore against a 3.5-4 lakh drawdown.
Scale into rescue in ladders (multiple strikes/quantities), not one desperate ticket.
Converting a losing directional short into a hedged combo (long future + sold call + sold puts) can cap damage.
Intraday 100+ point falls that recover are put-selling windows; retail sells first, institutions stabilize.

strategies.name: Short-stock rescue ladder (firefighting)
strategies.construction: Short future + sold call went wrong; rescue = sold puts at 4,500/4,700/4,800/4,900/5,000/5,200 (4,500 qty total) + long Jan future + sold 5,500 call
strategies.numbers: Stock +250 (4,900->5,150); drawdown 3.5-4 lakh; ~1 crore extra margin; ~10 lakh margin per 1,000 qty; result +1.49 lakh
strategies.best_regime: When a short directional view is hit by a gap/momentum move you believe is temporary
strategies.adjustments: Ladder put sales into the spike, convert to hedged combo, keep averaging only with reserve capital
strategies.risks: Requires massive reserve margin; if the rally continues, losses compound - works only with deep pockets and fast execution

quotes: I am not a God - many times my view has gone terribly wrong; it is the money power and the adjustment plan that save the trade.

summary: Nifty P/E hit a record 37.16 (P/B 3.82, dividend yield 1.18). Argues crash calls from P/E alone are wrong: P/E = price/EPS, and COVID-crushed EPS inflated the ratio. P/E can normalize via falling prices OR recovering earnings - shows Maruti EPS -8 to +46, ONGC collapse; if earnings double, P/E halves without any fall.
lessons: P/E has two levers: price and earnings; focusing on only one while predicting crashes is a category error.
Distressed EPS makes P/E meaningless (zero/negative earnings = infinite P/E at any price).
A ratio can normalize without a crash if earnings recover - the 2020 P/E spike was a denominator artifact.
Trend is your friend until it bends: do not short a market merely because a single valuation metric is stretched.
quotes: A ratio with two parameters cannot be judged by watching one - people watch price and ignore earnings.

summary: Guided tour of the NSE option chain (strike grid, bid/ask, LTP, IV, volume, open interest) and first payoff-chart walkthroughs: long 13,200CE at 170 (premium 12,750, breakeven 13,370, max loss = premium, ~29% probability of profit) and long 12,800PE at 186 (breakeven 12,614). Covers lot sizes, weekly index expiries and illiquidity of long-dated options as of Dec 2020.
lessons: Breakeven at expiry = strike plus premium for calls, strike minus premium for puts; profit territory begins only beyond breakeven.
Maximum loss for an option buyer is the premium paid; profit is uncapped for calls.
Weekly expiries existed on Nifty and Bank Nifty while stock options had only the monthly expiry; long-dated (5-year) index options exist but are illiquid.
Probability of profit for a typical slightly-OTM long option is around 30% - buyers lose most of the time by design.

quotes: You cannot do the betting for one share. You have to do a betting for 75 shares.

summary: Turn to caution: Nifty future high 14,660, then second-wave Friday selling (−140); Infosys/HCL fell despite beats; US banks (WFC/JPM/C) fell on good results; VIX India & US >24; inauguration-week fear; sold weekly 13,500 PE @₹10. HDFC Bank weekend results. Range 14,000–14,700; sold 14,800–15,000 calls.
lessons: When good results can't lift stocks, the market is positioned too bullish — time for caution, not prediction.
Friday risk is three-nights risk: weekend mistakes cost triple.

summary: Five broker-cheating methods from personal experience: inflated 'transaction charges' masking brokerage, illegal interest on collateral, per-share-vs-per-lot 'computer mistakes' (₹60,000 charged on two lots), percentage pledging fees vs CDSL's ₹5, and uncredited pay-in cheques.
lessons: Judge brokers by total cost per lot including transaction charges, never headline brokerage.
No interest can be charged on F&O collateral - it is an agreement settled by exchange margins, not a loan.
Check contract notes: a 'per lot' brokerage charged 'per share' multiplies by lot size.
Pledging should cost the CDSL rate (about ₹5-10), never a percentage of value.
quotes: Why do brokers' computers only make mistakes that move client money to the broker?

summary: Bloodbath: Sensex -1,000+ (18th time since 2015), Nifty -350 from high to 14,650, 20-DMA broken, ~30% of Nifty-50 down >3%, India VIX +15% above 25 (above US VIX). Plans cash buying via put-selling (BPCL, IOC, ITC, Sun TV ~5% below market); expects stabilization 14,400-14,700 (50-DMA). FII and DII both sold ~900cr.
lessons: Full-market panic is the investor's window: 'bull market is the time to sell your mistakes, bear market is the time to buy your ambitions.'
Sell puts below value zones and take delivery if assigned - converts panic into staged accumulation.

summary: Gap-up faded but HDFC results (+3%) turned an expected black Friday green. Tata Steel ran 500 to ~1,200 in a month. India VIX crashed over 5%. US April jobs shocked at 2.66 lakh vs 1 million expected; Dow fell but Nasdaq rose; yields down.
lessons: Retail buys bad news sectors (oxygen, masks, pharma) hoping to capitalize - the crowd chases the theme.
Buy-your-own-shares story: retail picking stocks alone buys the bad apples; expert filtering at least halves mistakes.

summary: A factory ships an empty soap box; engineers spend millions on a scanning system while a floor worker solves it with a high-velocity fan. Lessons: experience beats credentials; simple solutions beat sophisticated jargon (mocking 'knowledge dissemination industry' and 'delta hedging with gamma scalping' trainers); the market rewards simple, executable ideas.
lessons: Simple, executable solutions usually beat sophisticated ones - complexity is often performance theater.
Credentials do not impress the market; only P&L does.
Over-engineering a problem usually means it was framed wrong.
quotes: Does the stock market know you are from Stanford University?
Things are not complicated - we make them complicated.

summary: Point-by-point rebuttal to trolls citing an MCA-filed FY2019-20 loss for the speaker's trading company: publishes multi-year P&L across two company accounts (~₹11–14 crore cumulative), argues the loss year was an investment drawdown, defends workshop/PMS minimum-capital gates and donation record.
lessons: Only three types never lose in markets: the divine, liars, and Excel/Twitter traders.
An ITR rarely reveals trading P&L when income comes from many sources.
Corporate loans from directors are capital, not debt — a common misread of MCA filings.
Even professionals' single-year losses can equal one month of their average income — judge multi-year records, not one filing.

strategies.name: Capital gating (disclosed policy)
strategies.construction: Workshops: refuse participants below ₹25 lakh capital; managed accounts: ₹5 crore minimum
strategies.numbers: As stated
strategies.best_regime: Retail protection practice
strategies.adjustments: One-day workshops allowed at ₹10 lakh capital
strategies.risks: Excludes small accounts by design; framed as ethics, also excludes scrutiny

quotes: Only God, liars, and Excel traders never lose money in the stock market.
Don't play with the knife — the same knife is safe in an adult's hand; risk must match the handler.

summary: Teaches a credit-funded hedge: sell a deep-ITM September 17,000 straddle (~Rs 689) and buy a December 17,000 put (~Rs 678) so entry is net credit. One-month backtest: combined premium 1,174 to 572, net +Rs 72/share (~Rs 3,600/lot on ~Rs 1 lakh margin, ~3.6%/month); his actual entry returned ~1.27%/week (~66% annualized). Entry ~45 days out; adjustments are the real edge.
lessons: Enter hedged structures only on net credit: premium received must exceed protection paid - never pay out of pocket to open.
Buying protection in a far month instead of near OTM wings slashes hedge bleed while capping disaster risk.
The edge is not the entry but the adjustment workflow - most profit arrives while firefighting.
Annualize honestly: 3.6%/month is ~43% p.a., still above what most businesses earn - set expectations, not lottery hopes.

strategies.name: Deep-ITM short straddle with far-month protective put
strategies.construction: Sell ATM+1 deep-ITM straddle near month (Sept 17,000 CE+PE with spot ~16,500); buy same-strike put in far month (Dec 17,000 PE)
strategies.numbers: Entry ~45 days to expiry; Sept combined premium 689 vs Dec put 678 (net credit ~11); margin ~Rs 1 lakh/lot; 1-month backtest 1,174 to 572 = +72/share; ~3.6%/month or 66% annualized on actual trade
strategies.best_regime: Mildly bullish consolidation with elevated far-month IV; also works as directional view with disaster cap
strategies.adjustments: Roll/adjust the short legs as market moves; may add capital; far put stays as backstop
strategies.risks: Locks modest max profit; large fast moves cause MTM pain before adjustment; far-month put loses value if market drifts up slowly

quotes: If you are walking home it takes ten minutes; if a dog chases you, three - adjustments are where the profit is.

summary: Dollar index near 95 and 10Y yield above 1.56 trigger global risk-off; India fell ~1% vs Europe -2%. Institutions (FII -800cr, DII -999cr) both sold; retail absorbed. HDB Financial stake-sale news alone held up HDFC Bank. Speaker stays medium-term bullish: 18k by month-end if results good.
lessons: Do not trade on flash news planted to help someone exit - the Buffett-Kotak rumor is the cautionary case.
Being right 70-80% of the time is enough to make money; needing to be always right is a beginner's error.

summary: Fourth straight day of 200+ point intraday swings but Nifty closed green; ICICI Bank +11-12% on results single-handedly saved ~250-300 Nifty points; money rotated from HDFC Bank into ICICI; Reliance fell after results; Bank Nifty crossed 41,000.
lessons: A heavyweight's result day can swing Nifty by 250-300 points on its own
Consecutive 200-point intraday falls typically end in a violent recovery once institutions step in

summary: Post-results review of Adani group trades: ₹78 lakh profit in four months, but the real lesson is a 1,500PE position (77,000 qty) squared off at ₹3-4 one day before results; the stock fell >10% next day and the put went to ₹120 — an avoided ~₹80 lakh loss.
lessons: Option sellers eat like a hen and give back like an elephant: one unhedged event can erase months of profit.
Sitting in large profits just before a binary event (results) is a signal to bank them, unless the outcome is known.
Position size amplifies event risk: 77,000 quantity × a 10% stock move = ₹80 lakh, bigger than four months of profits.
Track aggregate exposure per underlying, not per trade — a 'small' 3-rupee put is not small at scale.
quotes: If you are an option seller sitting in good profit just ahead of results — come out, unless you are fairly sure of the outcome.

summary: A beginner trader ran crypto options on an unregulated exchange with a 2,000 USDT trading credit and returned ~45% in a month. Walks through crypto option mechanics: option-chain UI, wallet-vs-margin allocation, auto square-off, transfer fees, and P&L-report flaws.
lessons: Crypto premiums are ultra-high: the same far-OTM strikes that pay pennies on index options paid thousands of dollars.
Exchange P&L reports counted premium credits as profit; true P&L must be computed from wallet balance minus deposits.
Funds sit in a wallet and must be allocated to trading; unallocated losing positions get auto squared-off.
Cross-exchange USDT transfers cost $10-50 in network fees - a real drag for small accounts.

strategies.name: Crypto premium selling (beginner account)
strategies.construction: Sold BTC 55,000 put, bought 58,500 call; sold ETH 5,000 call (near expiry); sold BTC 48,000 put - all on a 2,000 USDT trading credit
strategies.numbers: Capital 2,000 USDT to ~2,900 in a month (~45%); gross 1,200, net 900 after ~300 in charges; BTC Mar-2022 100k call fell from ~5,000 to ~2,000; 20,000 put from ~500 to ~150; Dec 80,000 call ~687
strategies.best_regime: High-IV crypto markets; wide expected ranges
strategies.adjustments: None described - amateur discretionary selling
strategies.risks: Unregulated exchange, counterparty risk; premiums can expand violently (India ban news dropped local BTC/ETH 20% in a day); high fees

quotes: Sometimes markets tend to move violently. So that brings us to one question. What is the hedge that we have?

summary: Cautionary anatomy of a stock-option buyer: an IndusInd 450-strike put expired out-of-the-money by last-traded price but in-the-money by the weighted-average close, forcing physical settlement and an auction-market buyback near 480 - a ~13.5 lakh loss on a ~1 lakh premium.
lessons: 'Limited risk' buying is false for physically-settled stock options that expire ITM - losses can multiply many times the premium.
Closing price is the last half-hour weighted average, not the last traded price; strikes near the money hinge on this distinction.
Never carry stock options into expiry: square off at least a day early, or trade index options which are cash-settled.
quotes: Always remember, information is wealth... the risk can be unlimited even if you are an option buyer.

summary: Three market participants - arbitrageurs (now dominated by computer algorithms, making manual arbitrage very hard), speculators (99% of people) and hedgers (hedging still new to Indian traders).
lessons: Algorithms have taken over small arbitrage opportunities - manual arbitrage is now very difficult.
Hedging is still a new concept for most Indian traders; 99% of participants are pure speculators.
quotes: 99% of the people do only speculation. Hedging is something very new to Indian traders.

summary: Argues the war panic is really energy politics: Europe's gas dependence, Nord Stream 2 ($11B, 1,250 km), Germany supplying only 5,000 helmets, ~14,000 deaths since 2014 treated as routine; predicts pressure tactics over full-scale war; advises light positions and hedged far-OTM selling; flags 16,800 support and the 200-DMA held for a year.
lessons: Big conflicts are usually resource conflicts - identify the underlying commodity (here natural gas), not the headline.
'Fear of war is worse than war': prolonged pressure tactics depress markets more than the actual event.
Into headline-risk periods: keep positions light, sell only far-OTM options, buy a hedge for every short.
quotes: It's all about oil politics... it's all about natural gas politics.
Be prepared for a rollercoaster ride... the underlying problem is natural gas, not Ukraine.

summary: STT is paid whether you gain or lose; with more than 95% of participants losing money, loss-makers faithfully contribute to the government's tax kitty - no other Indian business taxes a person who is losing money.
lessons: STT applies on both sides regardless of profit or loss - a cost most beginners ignore.
Loss-makers still contribute tax revenue; no other Indian business is taxed while losing.

summary: Full-time trading demands financial backup, not 'financial freedom' fantasy: two friends with identical 50 lakh capital - a simple-liver survives, the EMI-laden earner does not. Bank-clerk-turned-trader story: 1 lakh stakes lost one after another. Infosys founder's wife-backup anecdote; the 90-90-90 saying; dividend income as a replacement salary only at very large capital.
lessons: Go full-time only with backup that lets you survive if the market capital goes to zero.
'Financial freedom' is marketing - even the wealthy keep working; markets reward long engagement, not escape.
Losing small stakes repeatedly ('just 1 lakh more') is how disciplined-looking people blow up.
Saying: 90% of participants lose 90% of capital in 90 sessions.
quotes: If I could make all poor people rich with good advice, nobody in the world would be poor.

summary: Live broker-platform walkthrough: login, dashboard P&L (including an open F&O loss shown honestly), portfolio view, pledging shares for margin, buying ETF units, watchlists, order placement, P&L and tax reports; message: master the few functions you actually use.
lessons: A broker platform is like a TV remote: 99% of the time you need only buy, sell, positions and P&L reports.
Pledging holdings converts the portfolio into trading margin in a few clicks.
Show your losses too - an honest P&L view includes open F&O drawdowns.
quotes: There are so many functionalities but the basic things we do are buy, sell and see the profit-loss statement.

summary: Two regulatory clarifications from primary documents: (1) SEBI circular of 20-Jul-2021, para 18 - the 50% cash-equivalent collateral rule applies at the clearing-member/broker level, NOT the client level; brokers demanding 50% cash from clients misrepresent it. (2) There is no 'peak margin penalty' or intraday penalty that may be charged to clients: per NSE FAQ and an SEBI RTI reply (Dec 2021), upfront-margin-shortfall penalties cannot be passed on; only end-of-day shortfall, with the broker first obliged to demand top-up. Includes an RTI-driven broker refund anecdote and the 5-session reporting-window exploitation.
lessons: Read the actual circular before accepting a broker's compliance claim.
Upfront-margin-shortfall penalties are the broker's liability, not a client pass-through; only EOD shortfall can be pursued after a top-up demand.
Unwinding one leg of a hedge by mistake converts it to naked and triggers margin shortfall - leg discipline is a margin risk.
Brokers can exploit the ~5-session reporting window; clients who know the rules recover wrongly charged penalties.
quotes: There is no such thing called peak margin penalty... there is only end-of-day margin penalty, and the broker must first ask you to top up.

summary: March-deadline tax planning explainer. ELSS under 80C (Rs.1.5 lakh): five mistakes - last-week lump-sum timing risk (prefer monthly SIP of ~12,500), yearly fund-hopping, redeeming right after the 3-year lock-in (hold 8-10 years for 12-15% vs FD 8-9%), mismatching fund market-cap style to risk profile, and chasing last year's winner instead of 5-10-year record vs benchmark. NPS: extra Rs.50,000 under 80CCD(1B); at retirement 60% withdrawable (tax-free), 40% must buy annuity; equity/debt mix chosen by age and risk.
lessons: Spread tax investments through the year - last-week lump sums carry pure timing risk.
One well-chosen fund beats a shelf of annual switches; monitor less, hold longer.
A 3-year lock-in is a minimum, not a horizon: mutual funds reward 8-10-year holds.
Choose ELSS market-cap style by risk profile; small caps pay in bulls and punish in bears.
quotes: We never study until one day before the exam - the same way we save tax only in the last week of March.

summary: Nifty -1% on week against green global markets; Canadian pension fund sold Kotak shares worth Rs 6,800 cr in a block deal. FII March selling Rs 47,000 cr - highest in a year. Reliance +20% (2,200 to 2,630) the lone pillar. Brent broke $100 then hit $123; Saudi Aramco refinery attack jolted Dow Friday. Consolidation 17,000-17,500 into expiry expected.
lessons: Mid/small-cap outperformance while the index falls shows the decline is concentrated in a few heavyweights.
Expiry weeks typically bring heavier FII selling - plan around the calendar.

summary: Annual performance review across multiple personal/family accounts: combined F&O profit ~Rs.17.6 crore (+~Rs.45 lakh broker-error refund ~ Rs.18.1 crore) on ~Rs.30-35 crore capital (~45-50% return), plus ~Rs.2 crore interest income ~ ~Rs.20 crore vs a Rs.25 crore expectation. Profit was concentrated in H1; option writers lost from September 2021 as volatility rose; March alone saw a >Rs.2 crore loss in one large bank stock. Sets Rs.100 crore corpus and Rs.50 crore next-year profit targets; announces a capital-gated mentorship program.
lessons: 35-40% per annum (3-4% monthly) is the honest expectation band for a professional option seller - no rat race with anyone.
Even good years are regime-dependent: profits concentrated in favorable months; a volatile regime can give back months of gains.
Large positions in single stocks (a trapped high-volume hedge) can cost crores in one month - size is destiny.
Illiquid far-expiry options are hard to reconstruct after a broker error - liquidity is part of position risk.
quotes: I don't compare myself with anybody... even if you make one rupee profit you are still in the top one percent of traders in India.

summary: A mild-bullish Infosys earnings trade (naked 1900CE sale plus 1600/1500PE spread) hit a post-results gap-down to 1550; rescue: book call and hedge profits, convert the 1600PE into a straddle by selling 1600CE; exited ~55K profit (~2.5-3% on ~20L).
lessons: No strategy works in all conditions - the adjustment process is the real skill.
Avoid carrying earnings risk into long weekends; a Friday mistake costs three nights of sleep (ADR falls overnight).
Selling a call into a gap-down panic converts a broken put position into a straddle with fat premium.

strategies.name: Infosys earnings rescue via straddle conversion
strategies.construction: Sell 1900CE x10 naked; sell 1600PE x10, buy 1500PE x10; on gap-down square calls (+21,600) and 1500PE (+7,000), sell 1600CE x10 to form straddle
strategies.numbers: ~20L margin; final ~55,000 profit (~2.5-3%) in 4-5 sessions; straddle net +30,000; break-evens 1520/1680
strategies.best_regime: Stock with multi-year support shelf into results
strategies.adjustments: Straddle held as insurance with prepared delivery/roll plan
strategies.risks: Continued slide through 1520 break-even

quotes: Sometimes firefighting is needed: if a dog chases me, I reach home in five minutes instead of thirty.

summary: Full anatomy of a rescued short-2200CE position in Adani Enterprises: stock ran 1800 to 2400; a ladder of put sales, a call ratio, straddles and strike-rolls turned a 7.03L loss into ~37L profit (incl. Adani Port strangle) in one month.
lessons: Never sit passively on a losing short option - move strikes and legs dynamically as the underlying travels.
Divide capital into 10-15 parallel strategies so rescue capital always exists without closing winners.
Return-on-investment framing misleads for collateral-based sellers; absolute profit and capital-at-risk both matter.

strategies.name: Adani Ent short-call rescue ladder
strategies.construction: Sell 2200CE at 1800 spot; then sell 1800/1900/2000/2040PE as price rises; buy 2100CE financed by selling 2300CE (call ratio); straddle 2240 with doubled 2240PE; later 2300PE, 2400CE, 2500CE
strategies.numbers: Initial call loss 7,03,000; put ladder +2,39,000/+2,26,000/+3,84,000/+4,80,000; ratio legs +5,00,000/+6,00,000; 2100PE +7,64,000; final ~35.7L plus 1.8L Adani Port strangle = ~37L
strategies.best_regime: Violently trending single stock - adjust with the trend
strategies.adjustments: Strike-rolls, ratio financing, doubling puts on extended moves
strategies.risks: Unhedged put ladder on reversal; doubling into a runaway trend

quotes: Being an option seller, you just don't take a position and sit down the whole month unless you believe in horoscope.

summary: Live construction of a September-expiry BTC structure: long 35k call ratio-financed (1:4) with 55k call sales plus split 20k/25k put sales; profit zone 24,600-62,500; rationale: IV collapsed to 65-70 so combos of cheap buys and sells beat naked shorts.
lessons: When IV is low, naked short straddles are poor value; buy cheap wings and finance with ratio sales instead.
Split surplus short quantity across two put strikes instead of stacking at one.
Long-dated expiries harvest range premium with fewer rolls.

strategies.name: BTC September ratio structure
strategies.numbers: Profit zone 24,600-62,500; BTC spot ~39,600; IV 65-70 vs 120-130 earlier
strategies.best_regime: Long multi-month range with mild bullish tilt
strategies.adjustments: Hold to September; follow-up planned
strategies.risks: Naked put tail below 24,600; upside slope flattens past 55k

quotes: When IV is low, your buy option is cheaper - so a combination will work out.

summary: Confesses a 1.31 crore loss in HDFC twins: a long future plus short 2400CE became a 2400 straddle the day before the merger announcement sent HDFC up 15% to 2950; escalating gap-down firefighting at 200-300 lots deepened losses despite ~90L month profit elsewhere.
lessons: Position sizing is the first Domino: oversized lots turned an adjustment into a disaster.
Sometimes firefighting pours petrol, not water - escalating into a violent mover compounds losses.
Markets show their true color when you are least prepared; size single-stock exposure assuming the surprise case.
Split capital across parallel strategies so rescue capital never requires closing winners.

strategies.name: HDFC merger straddle disaster (case study)
strategies.construction: Long HDFC future + short 2400CE; squared future, sold 2400PE -> short straddle; merger news -> +15% spike to 2950; repeated put sales and rolls while stock gap-downed daily
strategies.numbers: Net loss 1,31,85,828 in HDFC + ~1L profit in HDFC Bank; month P&L ~90L across three brokers vs 2Cr target
strategies.best_regime: Should never have been sized this large into a binary merger
strategies.adjustments: Escalating firefighting (200-300 lots) - the failure case
strategies.risks: Binary corporate actions on an oversized short straddle

quotes: Sometimes in the name of firefighting, instead of putting water into the fire, by mistake we put petrol.

summary: Debunks the viral FII-outflow claim: NSE daily figures are provisional (May-2022 cash selling 51,800cr provisional vs ~35,000cr SEBI-revised), and 12-year totals ignore primary-market inflows - IPO/QIP money adds 3.48L cr to 3.08L cr secondary net, ~6.56L cr total.
lessons: NSE same-day FII data is provisional; SEBI's T+1 revised data can differ by thousands of crore - always recheck.
Summing secondary-market flows ignores IPO/QIP subscriptions, overstating 'money leaving India'.
Bear-market thresholds: 0-10% noise, 10-20% correction, >20% bear market - Nifty was not yet there in May 2022.
quotes: As long as we have not fallen more than 20%, we are not in bear-market territory.

summary: Pre-CPI paralysis: US de-risking drove Dow -650 (last hour -400); SGX low 16,203 (~280 points below prior close, reacting more than US); FII shorts inched 75%->76% despite yesterday's +200 rally; Dow down 10 of last 11 weeks; expectation: US May CPI 8.3%, above = gap down 2-3%, below = relief; he refuses to take bearish bets before the data.
lessons: Ahead of binary events, traders de-risk: expect artificial selling in the last hour before big data.
If you make a mistake any day you lose one night's sleep; on a Friday you lose three - do not carry weekend risk.
A rally that comes only from short covering cannot be trusted; only post-data buying proves demand.

summary: Arguing India's F&O-to-cash volume ratio (~100x, world's highest, >90x from options) is dangerous, the speaker proposes banning stock futures (use margin funding to go long, stock lending & borrowing to short), allowing covered calls only against demat shares and cash-secured puts only at full margin, channeling speculation into indices.
lessons: Index derivatives are structurally hard to manipulate; stock derivatives enable bear-raids, collateral-value attacks and expiry-day games.
Leverage needs (long via margin funding, short via SLB) already exist without stock futures - and SLB would pay lenders (mutual funds, hence retail) extra yield.
F&O-to-cash turnover ratio of ~100x (options >90% of it) made India the world's most derivatives-heavy market.
quotes: Cash market should drive the futures market, but in India there is a possibility the futures market is driving the cash market.
Index being an average of so many stocks, manipulation is very, very difficult.

summary: Expiry-day preview amid global chaos: Dow making ~1000-point daily swings; Fed chair warned US may not avoid recession; UK inflation above 9%; FII June selling second-highest on record; rupee at fresh all-time low. Expects flat open and volatile expiry; 17,400-17,500 straddle (~150-160 premium) favored.
lessons: If FIIs park sale proceeds in Indian debt instruments, it signals correction-and-return; moving money out of India signals longer exit.
Expect 5-10% swings either way until inflation clarity emerges; position sizing must assume it.

summary: One-idea episode: the best advice is to not seek advice - take the plunge, gain experience, then improve system, psychology and position sizing. Experience is the best teacher.
lessons: Experience is the best teacher; motivational words cannot substitute screen time.
Improve three things iteratively: system, psychology, position sizing.
quotes: My best advice is that you do not seek any advice from anyone - take the plunge, get the experience, then improve the system, psychology and position sizing.

summary: The Delhi snake-bounty parable (Cobra effect): a government paying for dead snakes led to people farming snakes. Good intentions can create perverse incentives that worsen the original problem.
lessons: Incentives must be designed for the behavior you want, not the metric you pay for (Cobra effect).
Regulation and tax breaks often produce the opposite of the stated intent.

summary: Back from Bali; Nifty high 17,965 - 35 pts from 18,000, nearly all 2022 losses recovered; FIIs bought 11 straight sessions (+2,347cr) but only 1/10th of their 9-month selling - market's resilience; BN crossed 39,500 late; US retail sales non-event; Fed minutes next; Muthoot pick failed -10%, GNFC new pick.
lessons: The market can fully recover a year's losses on one-tenth of the selling that caused them - flows are a weak predictor of direction
Momentum picks without stops end like his Muthoot call: -10% in a day; always trade candidates with a stop loss

summary: Traces the standard failure arc: cash market impatience -> leveraged futures -> social-media advice -> technical-analysis workshop -> overleveraged blowup on a news gap -> overcorrection to tiny size -> tiny portfolio returns. Conclusion: success is margin management, not indicators.
lessons: Technical analysis is part of a trading system, not the heart of it - over-reliance on charts is a failure signature.
Futures are pure leverage: a 1% price move is a ~10% move on margin; novices see only the upside.
In India, gaps make stop-losses unreliable for positional trades - overnight news can blow through any stop.
Overcorrecting to tiny size after a blowup produces 10% return on 20% of capital = 2% portfolio return; ROCE and portfolio return are different things.
quotes: Futures have no futures, options have plenty of options.
The success of the trader lies not in his technical analysis skill but in managing his margin money efficiently.

summary: Advises informed decisions over blind news-following; closes with the classic exchange between money and experience in markets.
lessons: Research before buying - do not follow news blindly; markets transfer money from the inexperienced to the experienced over time.
quotes: Stock market is the place where people with money meet people with experience, and after some time the people with experience become people with money.

summary: ECB 75bp done; Powell's mid-session speech read as less hawkish and US recovered with a +0.5% last-10-minutes burst. Now Nasdaq, S&P, Nifty and Bank Nifty are all technically long - but chasing 200 points after the signal risks buying the top. IT is 20-30% off highs vs banks near highs. Weekend logic: Friday mistakes cost three nights of sleep. Disbelief sustains rallies.
lessons: A 'technically long' signal is an entry zone, not a chase confirmation - enter near the trigger or wait for a pullback.
Rallies persist while disbelief persists; the crowd's entry marks the top.

summary: Compact contrast of option buyer vs seller: buyer pays small premium in cash with low win probability; seller posts large margin but can fund it with collateral; buyer can be right on direction yet lose to premium decay, while seller can be wrong on view yet still profit if price stays inside breakevens.
lessons: The seller's edge is statistical cushion: being wrong on direction but right on range still pays.
Buyers risk capital in cash; sellers can post collateral — a capital-efficiency asymmetry few beginners grasp.
quotes: Option buyer his view may go correct, still he can lose... option seller his view can go wrong and still he can make money.

summary: Hong Kong hit a fresh 52-week low (~18,500 from 26,000+); Fed funds futures 82% for a 75bp hike; hourly RSI below 30 invites technical bounces; windfall/export duty cuts on diesel and ATF help Reliance; advice: go very light into the Fed event.
lessons: Position sizing is the real stress management: too many positions into a binary event guarantees emotional errors.
When hourly RSI is under 30, sell call options into bounces rather than chasing shorts.

summary: Apple fell 5% on reports it dropped plans to make 6 million extra iPhone 14 units - the last leg of capitulation he argues; FIIs entered October 87% net short in index futures (a record); rupee hit 82; he is selling cash-secured puts (TCS 2,800 / Infy 1,300 / RIL 2,200) ready for delivery.
lessons: When the bluest blue chip capitulates 5% on its own demand news, the selling cycle is typically near its end.
Being 87% short, FIIs are the fuel for any violent squeeze - positioning extremes predict the next move's direction, not its timing.

summary: Intraday short-strangle money managers charge layered costs clients never see: at 10 lakh capital, ~15 straddle lots doubled into 120 lots/day at 12 rupees/lot brokerage = 4.5 lakh/year, plus ~3 lakh STT/stamp duty and ~2.5 lakh slippage - the entire 10 lakh capital consumed annually. The manager's own account pays almost nothing, so posted returns are an illusion.
lessons: Run the full cost stack (brokerage x lots x round trips + STT/stamp duty + slippage) before believing any intraday return claim.
A manager trading his own account with near-zero negotiated costs can show 70%+ annual returns that are structurally impossible for clients paying retail costs.
If easy money exists, the broker takes it, the government takes it, and the manager takes the rest - the client gets peanuts.

strategies.name: Cost-audit of a typical intraday iron-fly money-manager operation
strategies.construction: Sell ATM straddle + buy 1,000-1,500 point wings (Bank Nifty ~39,100); ~60,000 margin per lot set; 15 lot sets on 10 lakh capital; squared off daily
strategies.numbers: 120 lots/day x 12 rupees brokerage = ~1,800/day = 4.5 lakh/year; STT+stamp ~3 lakh/year; slippage ~2.5 lakh/year; total ~10 lakh = entire capital; manager's own equivalent costs ~1,000/month
strategies.best_regime: Audit template for anyone evaluating a money manager
strategies.adjustments: N/A
strategies.risks: Client returns are negative before strategy risk even begins

quotes: If there is easy money, the broker will take away... the government will take away, and your fund manager will take away everything - what you get is a peanut.

summary: How staged P&L screenshots work: buy options in one account, take an equal short in another - post only the winning account's screenshot; losses go silent. Detection heuristics: unreasonable returns, unchanged capital, lifestyle that contradicts claimed wealth. Includes the 50k-to-30-lakhs-in-6-months conference claim and a regulator reportedly forcing one influencer to stop posting P&Ls.
lessons: Selective posting of one account while an opposite account absorbs losses is the classic fake-P&L structure - audit capital growth and lifestyle, not screenshots.
A trader claiming crores in profit whose capital never compounds and who still rides a bus is running a display, not a business.
Screenshots create greed; greed is the product being sold - workshops and tip channels monetize it.
Even charity is part of a credible wealth story: verifiable contribution distinguishes real wealth from claimed wealth.
quotes: People don't want to get rich slowly, they want to get rich fast - that's why they lose money in the stock market.
If you are not humble, the market will make you humble.

summary: Technicians extrapolating 2008 and 2020 (crash then +110-120% in 12-15 months) project Nifty 35,000 by end-2023 from the June 2022 low of ~15,200. The speaker argues 99.99% against it: 2008/2020 recoveries rode 0% rates and QE; 2022 has a hiking Fed and QT. Lesson: be a techno-fundamentalist. Includes an REC bonus-issue anecdote destroying a mean-reversion trade, and two December-2023 long-dated strategies shown at a Dubai conference.
lessons: Pattern-matching past crashes fails when the policy regime differs: 2008/2020 recoveries needed 0% rates + QE; 2022 had rising rates + QT.
Do not be a pure technician or pure fundamentalist - be a techno-fundamentalist; charts plus macro context.
Mean reversion breaks on corporate actions: REC's fall from 140 to 105 was a 1:3 bonus adjustment, not a correction - the retracement trade expired worthless.
Long-dated option combos can carry wide breakevens and produce windfall months, but 'you cannot make this kind of profit every time'.

strategies.name: Dec-2023 18,000 short straddle (demonstration size)

strategies.adjustments: Not stated

strategies.adjustments: Rolledputs mentioned in related trades

If any technical analyst looks at the chart pattern of 2008 and 2020, he will assume 30,000-35,000. But there is a catch.

summary: Calm before the Fed: market consolidated, VIX rose into the event (event-driven, not fear). DIIs turned sellers (1,378 crore) nearly matching FII buys (1,436 crore); ADP jobs beat pushed US futures down; Vedanta and metals oddly strong despite bad results. 'Only three things matter tomorrow: the Fed, the Fed, and the Fed.'
lessons: Event-driven VIX spikes are mechanical, not fear - VIX typically deflates after the event regardless of direction.
Ahead of a binary event, flow data and positioning lose predictive value - stop analyzing, start waiting.

summary: PSU bank index returned ~20% in a year when Nifty managed 1.2%, accelerating to ~32% over 12 months after Canara Bank's ~88% profit jump; IBC resolutions and PCA cleanup drive re-rating. PSU banks still trade below book (Bank of Baroda 0.93) vs 3-4x for private banks; suggests PSU bank ETFs over funds, with a SIP-on-dips entry; closes with the 5-10% position-sizing rule after Vauld blame.
lessons: Stocks below book value with improving balance sheets offer re-rating upside with limited downside.
IBC resolutions and regulatory cleanups (PCA) set up multi-year re-rating cycles in beaten-down sectors.
Prefer low-cost ETFs over mutual funds for sector bets; buy via SIP and add on 5-10% dips.
Cap any single risky instrument at 5-10% of portfolio so a total loss is survivable.

strategies.name: PSU bank value + ETF entry
strategies.construction: PSU Bank BeES ETF (or PSU equity fund); SIP with added buying on 5-10% corrections
strategies.numbers: PSU bank index +20% (Nov 21-Nov 22) and +32% (Nov 21-Nov 18, 2022) vs Nifty +1.2%/+2%; private banks +2.8%; Bank of Baroda P/B 0.93 vs HDFC 3.6x, ICICI 3.5x, Kotak 4x; speaker's own ETF position ~+40%
strategies.best_regime: Early re-rating phase after cleanup; low P/B with improving profitability
strategies.adjustments: Add on dips rather than chase; expect low dividends from PSU banks (unlike PFC/REC/Coal India)
strategies.risks: Sector concentration; entry near market all-time highs; re-rating may stall

quotes: A stock that is going up will continue to go up... until you go bankrupt. Basically, what has happened - IBC has helped many banks.
If you have put only 10 percent of your portfolio, even if it has gone to zero, you are just losing only 10 percent.

summary: China unrest at Foxconn's Zhengzhou iPhone plant hits Apple supply; HK -4%, SGX -80/90. Weekend-risk advice: don't carry unhedged positions into weekends. 18,300 strong support (highest PE OI); month range 18,000-19,000. Crude broke $82 on China demand destruction. Future premium 150 must normalize (normal 40-60). IT focus; China pain may be India's gain.
lessons: Don't carry unhedged positions over weekends - mistakes on Friday cost three nights of sleep.
When futures premium is extraordinary, spot usually falls toward the future to normalize it.

summary: Jittery worldwide ahead of US CPI and Fed; SGX at Friday's low; FII sold >4,000cr in the week, DII bought >3,500cr; Infosys/Wipro ADR pressure; HDFC Bank ADR +1%; macro calm: crude $120->$76-77, rupee stable 81-83; support 18,400, day range 18,400-18,600 expected.
lessons: December is a seasonally lackluster month for FIIs (year-end book closing); fresh country allocations typically come in January
Index ADRs (Infosys, Wipro, HDFC Bank) are an overnight read-through for the Indian open

summary: Three real ruin stories against MTM-screenshot culture: Jesse Livermore's bankruptcy and suicide; a villager who borrowed from his village at 6%/month to ride the 2008-11 gold bull on 5% margin and was wiped out by one 10% overnight gold crash, then jailed; Nick Leeson and Barings (Kobe earthquake gap down, bank sold for £1).
lessons: Only bring to the market what you can afford to lose entirely.
5% commodity margin means a 10% adverse move can wipe 200% of capital in one session.
A full year of posted profits proves nothing about future survival; risk is risk.
Investors taking delivery can survive any fall; leveraged traders with expiry deadlines cannot.
quotes: Even a person may show MTM profit for one continuous year, but still it does not guarantee that he will be making only profit forever.
How much money you are ready to lose, that much money you can bring to the stock market.

summary: Bus-and-pothole parable on blindly following big traders, then two freak-event case studies: the 2012 freak trade where a dealer's misunderstood order crashed Nifty ~15% in seconds before reversal, and an expiry-day surgical-strike headline that gap-shocked options; warns that stop losses jump in gaps and big-quantity traders need hidden backup capital.
lessons: You cannot follow a big trader blindly; their size, margins and backup capital are invisible.
Stop losses jump over gaps - in a black swan your loss can exceed capital.
A single mistyped order can crash the index 15% in seconds before exchange intervention.
Exchange surveillance can trace and reverse freak trades, but option sellers' damage is already done.
quotes: Amateurs follow the bus into the pothole; the bus escapes, the motorbike does not.

summary: 2022 review: Nifty +4-5% but rupee -11-12% (negative in dollars); Dow -9%, S&P -20%, Nasdaq -33%, Tesla -65-70%, blue chips -50%; Bank Nifty +20-21% (PSU banks +60-70%), IT -25%, auto +15%, pharma -12%. Frames 2022 as a once-in-decade volatility year via the 1929/1991/2000/2008/2020 crisis cycle.
lessons: Judge annual performance in currency-adjusted terms; +5% Nifty with -11% rupee is a down year.
Roughly once a decade a major crisis hits (1991, 2000, 2008, 2020) - position sizing must assume it.
When everything is well, that is the time to sell; persisting worries power bull markets.
Worst sectors of a crash year (IT) and best (PSU banks) set up next year's rotation candidates.
quotes: When everything is well, that is a time to sell.

summary: Macro picture turning: China Q4 GDP beat, gas down, US inflation down to 6.5%, Fed funds futures ~95% odds of a 25bp hike. India's only problem remains FIIs (17 straight sell days). Recalls 2015: when Nifty was 15-18% down, LIC reportedly stepped in one day, +250-300 points (~4-5%), and that low never retested - capitulation needs one large buyer. ICICI/HDFC Bank ADRs +1%+; windfall-tax cut sentimentally aids RIL; above 18,000 the 18,000CE writers must cover.
lessons: Capitulation lows form when one large domestic buyer (SBI/LIC-class) steps in - watch for that signature
Strong global macro plus local FII selling is a lag, not a ledger - India typically catches up violently

summary: Budget eve: 'nearing the climax'. Bank Nifty already ~10% off the high; FPO path: subscribe / revise price / extend deadline / combination - decision expected by day end. Parliament commotion expected (BBC documentary + Adani) but budget should pass on time; budget uncertainty starts tomorrow, Fed after. Range 17,400-17,800 with violent late-day moves; 'stop loss is slow poison, no stop loss is quick poison'; best advice: stay away 2-3 days.
lessons: Markets can absorb good or bad news, but not uncertainty - name the uncertainty before sizing any trade
In event weeks, 'no position' is a position

summary: Powell's dovish remarks sent Dow +600; gap-up, short covering into 10,880. November's 5-week series ran 10,030 to 10,880 (~9%); HUL, L&T, HDFC, HDFC Bank +10-20%. 'Markets climb the wall of worries' - buy uncertainty, sell clarity. Bank Nifty 24,400 to 27,000. December risks: OPEC, US-China, state elections; positions kept light.
lessons: Buy when uncertainty is high and prices cheap; sell when everything is clear and prices high.

summary: Explains the violent up-move anomaly: strangle sellers trapped by a ~10% rally are forced to buy back far puts to free margin and re-sell closer strikes - creating put-premium distortion. Never deploy all margin; short strangle is the most dangerous strategy.
lessons: In violent moves, premiums behave abnormally because losing-side sellers are forced to square up and roll - not because the market 'should' behave that way.
Never deploy all margin in a strangle; spare cash lets you sell closer strikes without buying back the far leg at the worst price.
Short strangle is called the most dangerous strategy - unlimited one-sided loss with both legs naked.
Margin-release mechanics (square far leg, sell nearer leg) explain bid-ask distortions during panics.

strategies.name: Strangle roll-under-stress mechanics
strategies.construction: Short 9,000CE + 7,000PE written Friday around spot 8,000; on a violent rally, buy back 7,000PE (releasing margin) and sell 7,500/8,000PE instead
strategies.numbers: Legs 1,000 points either side of spot; roll targets 500-1,000 points closer
strategies.best_regime: After violent directional moves when the losing leg must be repositioned
strategies.adjustments: Roll the losing short leg closer using either spare cash (preferred) or margin released by squaring the far leg
strategies.risks: Forced buyback at inflated premiums; whipsaw if the market reverses immediately

quotes: Always remember, when markets move violently, do not expect option premiums to behave in the normal course.

summary: Teaches the cash-secured put end to end: sell a put at a strike you are happy to own, collect premium, take delivery if assigned. Shows live positions (Bajaj Finance, IndusInd, Nifty puts) and a claimed Rs.45 lakh FY21 profit in three weeks.
lessons: Sell puts only at prices where you are happy to take delivery - the premium is income, the strike is your target entry.
Far-month puts pay large premiums and give delivery intent when the market reaches your buy zone.
Squaring off and buying in the open market is usually cleaner than waiting for physical settlement.

strategies.name: Cash Secured Put
strategies.construction: Sell a put at the strike where you want to own the stock; keep the full cash ready for delivery
strategies.numbers: Bajaj Finance 1800PE sold at Rs.100 (2 lots, Rs.50,000 collected); Nifty Apr 7500PE ~Rs.57; Dec-2020 6000PE ~Rs.200; ~Rs.19 lakh premium collected; claimed Rs.45 lakh FY21 P&L in 3 weeks
strategies.best_regime: Sideways-to-up markets, or when you want a lower entry price in a quality stock
strategies.adjustments: Square off the put and buy shares in the open market instead of physical delivery; exit any time before expiry
strategies.risks: Profit capped at premium; stock can fall far below strike; requires full cash backing of the strike

quotes: If you are prepared to take delivery and the price does not fall below the strike, every month you can be making money.
When you square off and buy from the market, it is as good as buying at strike minus premium collected.

summary: Pre-results Infosys structure: short straddle at 650, converted to an iron fly with long 720CE/580PE wings, wings financed by selling double quantity of 750CE and 550PE. Payoff: max ~Rs.3.58 lakh (15%) at 650, protection zones 710/590.
lessons: Enter earnings trades the day before results and exit once the event resolves; hold further only with a stop-loss.
Finance protective wings by selling double quantity of farther strikes so the hedge costs nothing from pocket.
A naked short straddle is high risk; the same view becomes limited-risk when converted to an iron fly.

strategies.name: Infosys earnings iron fly with financed wings
strategies.construction: Sell 650CE + 650PE (5 lots); buy 720CE + 580PE; sell 2x 750CE (10 lots) and 2x 550PE to finance the wings

strategies.best_regime: Results eve with elevated implied volatility
strategies.adjustments: Exit after results or keep far wings with a stop-loss; watch volatility crush
strategies.risks: Beyond 750/550 the financing legs turn the risk unlimited again; overnight gap risk

quotes: This is the second strategy, iron fly - a limited risk strategy.
I do not want to pay from my pocket to buy the 720 call, so I sold double quantity of the 750 call.

summary: Contrasts results timing and IV: Infosys declares after hours (ATM IV ~67) while IndusInd declares intraday (ATM IV ~140). Plan: sell May-series 400CE+400PE straddle, hedge with current-month 500CE/300PE; net ~Rs.94.55/share (Rs.37,800/lot) on ~Rs.60,000 margin.
lessons: For high-IV stocks, sell the next-month straddle - richer premium with relatively smaller risk - and hedge with current-month wings.
Results timing matters: after-hours declarations carry gap risk, intraday declarations let you react.
ATM IV doubling between a quiet IT major and a volatile bank shows why event trades must be sized by IV, not by price.

quotes: One month is a very long time in trading.
In IndusInd, the long strangle can be in the current month to reduce the cost.

summary: Argues index options beat stock options: indices cannot crash 50-60% in a day (DHFL -65%, Infibeam -70% did), index margins are half of stock margins for similar contract size, far-strike liquidity is deep, no physical delivery, panic exits always available.
lessons: Return on margin matters, not how much the underlying moves - index gives 6-7% on margin vs 4% for a stock moving twice as much
Stocks can gap 50-70% overnight; indices are circuit-protected
Index options keep liquidity in far strikes and later months; stock options do not
No physical delivery headache in index options
quotes: At the end of the day, what matters is the return on our investment. It is not how many percent the underlying moves.

summary: Monthly P&L review: April profit 66.3 lakh on ~95 lakh starting capital after 45 lakh in first two weeks; attributes windfall to India VIX collapse 80-85 to ~40 and Nifty clearing the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement (9300-9400) toward 9900-10000; March also +50 lakh selling calls.
lessons: High collapsing VIX plus a clear directional view is where option sellers make windfall profits - not repeatable monthly
Know when to exit: he closed nearly all positions after the Fibonacci target hit
Markets factor in known bad news (efficient market) - shorting after visible bad news is how traders get squeezed
A trader can profit in a falling market and lose in a rising one - the view matters, not the market's direction

strategies.name: Put-selling ladder in collapsing-VIX rebound

strategies.adjustments: not detailed in this episode
strategies.risks: windfall not repeatable; VIX normalizes; requires conviction view

quotes: A trader can make profit even in a falling market and lose money even in a rising market - it is the view of the trader that is more important.
Markets are irrational and can continue to be irrational until you go bankrupt.

summary: Live pre-earnings trade: buy 1 lot 350CE (~2,440) and sell 2 lots 380CE (~1,190) - near-zero cost ratio. Max profit if ICICI closes 350-380 (month high 392, resistance 390-400), downside loss capped ~825, risk only above 410.
lessons: Structure pre-earnings trades around the stock's one-month high/low band
Buying 1 and selling 2 at a higher strike creates a near-zero-cost position with capped downside
Far-out risk (above 410) is acceptable only when the stock has shown no ability to get there

strategies.best_regime: mildly bullish stock pinned below known resistance into results
strategies.adjustments: not shown in this episode; speaker flags adjustment need if it gaps above 410

summary: First Q&A: stop-loss doctrine (slow poison vs quick poison), square-off vs counter-strategy depends on extra capital and skill, discount vs full-service brokers, basket/simultaneous orders, the 50% cash-equivalent rule applied at broker level, Bharat Bond/Liquid BeES as cash equivalents, hedging without adjustments is risky.
lessons: Stop-loss is non-negotiable: hit it and you can recover; blow up and you cannot (slow poison vs quick poison)
Square-off vs counter-strategy is decided by two questions: do you have additional capital and additional skill?
The 50% cash-equivalent requirement applies at broker level; brokers may pass it to clients (Zerodha does)
Cash equivalents: FD, Liquid BeES, liquid funds; Bharat Bond (~5% haircut) may qualify with some brokers
quotes: If you put a stop loss, it is like slow poison. If you don't put a stop loss, it is like quick poison.
If you lose part of the capital, you can hope to recover. But if you lose all the capital, you can never recover.

summary: Firefighting walkthrough on an ICICI Bank call-ratio position after a results miss: original 350/380 call spread risked ~Rs 0.50/share; by selling 400CE at 3.65 once the stock weakened, the position flipped to net credit and profit. Advises small traders to stick to indices.
lessons: When a thesis breaks, sell a further OTM option to convert the position into a net credit instead of accepting the planned loss.
Stock options move violently; small-capital traders should stick to indices.
Announce the risk of a trade before the event, then adjust mechanically after - not emotionally.

strategies.name: OTM credit-sale adjustment on a losing ratio
strategies.construction: Existing: long 350CE, short 2x 380CE (max loss ~0.50/share ~ Rs 800/lot). Adjustment: sell 1x 400CE at ~3.65
strategies.numbers: Pre-adjustment loss ~Rs 3,000; post-adjustment profit ~Rs 2,000 per lot
strategies.best_regime: After a results miss confirms the directional view is dead
strategies.adjustments: Collected credit exceeds the defined max loss; no further action needed unless stock reverses hard
strategies.risks: New short call adds upside risk; acceptable because view is now neutral-bearish

summary: Century-scale argument against crash calls: 100 years of Dow history shows every major crash (1929 ~90%, dot-com, Lehman) was followed by a powerful rebound; India's 1992/2000/2008/2020 parallels; Nifty PE ~16 sits in the historical buy zone (15-16) vs 28-30 sell zone; advises staggered ETF investing and cash-secured puts; '7500 bottom already made'.
lessons: Markets are unpredictable short-term but mean-revert upward across decades - every crash has been the entry for the next bull.
PE 15-16 has historically been an accumulation zone; 28-30 a distribution zone for Indian indices.
Contrarians win long-term; momentum target-setting is a different game - know which one you are playing.
Prefer broad ETFs over stock-picking unless you can dissect financials.

strategies.name: Staggered index investing with cash-secured puts
strategies.construction: SIP into a Nifty 50 ETF; optionally place cash-secured puts at desired lower entries
strategies.numbers: Nifty PE ~16 (May 2020); historical buy zone 15-16, sell zone 28-30; Dow 1929 crash ~90%; 1982-2000 bull ~15x
strategies.best_regime: Post-crash pessimism; long horizon
strategies.adjustments: Add on further 5-10% falls
strategies.risks: Multi-year drawdowns; requires no-liquidity-needs capital

quotes: A bull market is born out of pessimism, grows out of skepticism, matures out of optimism and dies out of euphoria.

summary: Q&A clarifying mechanics: buy/sell quantities are always equal (TV 'delivery buying' is interpretation); futures settle daily via MTM while option sellers' margin = span + premium value, rising with the option price; NSE uses a 10% risk-free rate in IV; June-2020 hedged margins ~one-third of naked; expiry settlement uses last-half-hour weighted average, not last traded price.
lessons: Futures: daily MTM cash transfer. Options: buyer pays premium once; seller's margin floats with the option's price.
Expiry settlement price is the weighted average of the last half hour - an ITM option can expire worthless despite a favorable last traded price.
Hedged option positions carry roughly one-third the margin of naked shorts (June 2020 regime).
Crowd consensus is dangerous: markets are structured so only the minority profits.

summary: Q&A: age-percentage debt rule and SIP/SWP for a retiree down 35%; short straddle as favorite strategy; ITM stock options must be squared off (physical delivery) while index options settle in cash at the half-hour VWAP; prefer LEAPS for low-monitoring office-goers; square off OTM options at 5 paise for clean tax statements; India lacks hedge funds because AIF Cat III has no tax pass-through; never sell options expiring the next day.
lessons: Keep roughly your-age-percent in debt; deploy lump sums via SIP, withdraw via SWP.
Trade indices, not stocks: ITM stock options that lapse trigger physical delivery; index options are cash-settled.
Sell options with enough time to expiry - next-day expiry invites gap risk you cannot hedge after the fact.
Square off even worthless shorts for clean broker statements and smoother income-tax scrutiny.

summary: Walks through SEBI's new margining on real examples: naked ATM options now ~1.0-1.3 lakh (up from 80-90k), but hedged spreads collapse to ~25-35k, cross-margined straddles to ~1.05 lakh, straddle-with-wings to ~45-55k, and an ITM put calendar under 30k - pushing traders toward hedged, index, defined-risk structures.
lessons: Under the new framework the margin system itself pays you to hedge: protection 200-300 points away cuts margin ~70%.
Cross-margining makes a short straddle cost little more than its single costlier leg - portfolio margin logic arrives in India.
Margin relief can seduce into over-sizing: four lots at 300-point risk recreates 1,200 points of exposure. Options trading is risk and position management, not strike selection.
Index exposure carries structurally lower margins (2% vs 3.5% exposure) - another argument to avoid stock options.

strategies.name: Hedged short option (spread)

strategies.best_regime: any directional credit view
strategies.adjustments: roll wings as market trends
strategies.risks: max loss = width x lot; premium give-up

strategies.numbers: margin ~45,000-55,000 after ~40-60k premium receivable; straddle premium >1,000 pts in July 2020

strategies.construction: Sell 10,000PE current month, buy 10,000PE next month

strategies.best_regime: neutral-to-mildly-bearish
strategies.adjustments: roll short leg at expiry
strategies.risks: fast rallies inflate long-leg decay loss

quotes: Options trading is not about which strike you sell - it is about risk management, margin management and position sizing.

summary: Contrasts the two flagship ETFs: Nifty BeES = equity (index returns, dividends rare - last in 2015), Liquid BeES = debt in government securities with interest paid as additional units, price pinned at ~1,000, and no STT/stamp duty/exchange charges; notes the collateral-haircut irony (5% for equity vs 10% for the risk-free debt product).
lessons: Liquid BeES functions as cash-equivalent collateral: interest accrues as extra units, price pinned near 1,000, zero STT/stamp duty.
India's collateral-haircut paradox: risky equity ETF gets 5% haircut while government-debt Liquid BeES gets 10% - know the rules before pledging.
For parking trading capital, frictionless debt ETFs beat idle cash that earns nothing.

strategies.name: Liquid BeES cash-component collateral
strategies.construction: Buy Liquid BeES; pledge as the cash component of margin
strategies.numbers: price ~1,000 +/- 1 paisa; interest via additional units monthly; no STT/stamp duty
strategies.best_regime: any time idle capital sits in a trading account
strategies.adjustments: n/a
strategies.risks: haircut 10%; liquidity depth

quotes: In computing they say what you see is what you get - Liquid BeES is exactly that: you pay 1,000, you get one unit.

summary: Euphoric gap-up morning (Nifty +200, Bank Nifty +500) fizzled: pre-market blog call that Nifty future would break 10,200 at least once played out; session closed as a Doji via the weighted-average close; RBI nod for IndusInd open-market buys lifted it early while HDFC/Kotak/Reliance were sold hard from highs; FII +813 cr vs DII -1,238 cr; view: consolidation with positive bias, supports 9,900/9,700.
lessons: Euphoric gaps attract profit-booking: 'a bull market dies of euphoria' - fade the open, respect the close.
The printed close is a last-half-hour weighted average - comparing it to yesterday's true close can fake a 'Doji' or fake momentum.
When a stock sets all-time highs and is still sold into strength, the positives are priced - supply beats narrative.
Stated supports belong to risk classes: 9,900 for aggressive traders, 9,700 for moderate - sizing follows the classification.
quotes: A bull market is born out of pessimism, grows out of skepticism, matures out of optimism and dies out of euphoria.

summary: Q&A session: hedging as non-negotiable doctrine, SEBI lot-size revision mechanics, collateral/pledging differences across brokers, expiry-day-only intraday selling, pre-market mechanics, and repeated refusals to comment on unhedged directional follower positions.
lessons: Always pair an option sale with an option purchase: margin drops sharply and black-swan loss is capped.
Lot sizes are revised to keep contract value inside the SEBI band of 5-10 lakh, reviewed every six months.
Intraday option selling only on expiry day, when far out-of-the-money options decay to zero.
If you cannot explain what happens to premium when you exit, you are not ready to trade options.

strategies.name: Hedged short put

strategies.best_regime: Any short-put view; mandatory insurance

summary: Post-market: overnight Dow futures -1000+ triggered bank-led selling (ICICI -5.5%); FII streak-selling 6000+ crore in four sessions; India VIX +5.69% above 30; speaker sold 1600 puts hedged with 1500 puts and Bank Nifty call ladder 21500-23000; range view 9500 support / 10350-10500 resistance.
lessons: FIIs buy in streaks and sell in streaks; the risk-on/risk-off flip, not the level, creates volatility.
VIX above 30 signals a high-volatility regime: violent intraday swings inside a stable range.
Whenever you sell an option, buy one too - margin falls and black swans are insured.

strategies.construction: Sell 1600 put, buy 1500 put (June expiry); Bank Nifty call ladder 21500/22000/22500/23000 with weekly hedges
strategies.numbers: FII context: -6000 crore in 4 sessions; VIX 30+

summary: Explains SEBI's cash-market margin changes effective 1 August 2020: upfront margin now required even to sell shares already held, because the exchange cannot distinguish intraday sells from delivery sells. Never take leveraged futures positions on a dividend-yield recommendation - leverage changes the whole risk of the idea
Crude futures curve pricing years ahead near current spot implies oil-marketing companies face no input-cost shock
Two disciplined entries for dividend stocks: cash-secured puts (willing to take delivery) or cash shares plus covered calls

strategies.name: Cash-secured put entry on BPCL
strategies.construction: Sell 350 put at ~14 while holding cash for delivery
strategies.numbers: strike 350, premium 14; delivery preferred below 336
strategies.best_regime: wanting the stock at an effective discount
strategies.adjustments: take delivery if assigned; keep premium otherwise
strategies.risks: stock can fall far below breakeven 336

quotes: The more the price goes down, the more the dividend yield and the more institutions will show interest

summary: Foundational lesson: derivatives defined via milk-to-butter and crude-to-petrol analogies; farmer price-realization origin story; >90% of Indian turnover is derivatives and Nifty is the world's most-traded contract; five derivative types; forward contracts taught through an exporter-student dollar exchange example.
lessons: A derivative's price is derived from an underlying - curd from milk, petrol from crude; keep the chain of derivation in mind
Derivatives began as farm price insurance (harvest-time glut) before entering financial markets after 1970
A forward fixes price today for a future exchange - each side eliminates the currency risk the other cannot bear
In India, derivatives turnover is 9x the cash market; Nifty is the world's most-traded derivative contract
quotes: Milk is the underlying, curd is the derivative; buttermilk is a derivative of curd

summary: Classifies derivatives participants into arbitrageurs, hedgers, speculators; teaches arbitrage via the tomato two-price example and the old inter-exchange (BSE-Madras) trade; personal 1995 story: borrowing at 3% in Singapore to park in 20% NRNR deposits, currency risk hedged with a forward at ~2%/yr cost, netting ~15% riskless.
lessons: Arbitrage = buy where cheap, sell where dear, simultaneously; technology and algos have closed the old manual inter-exchange gaps
Borrow low in one currency, deposit high in another, and hedge the currency leg with a forward - the residual is near-riskless carry
Hedging a carry trade costs something (here ~2%/yr); the true arbitrage is the spread minus the hedge cost
Speculators take directional risk and provide the liquidity that hedgers and arbitrageurs need

strategies.name: Covered interest carry trade (1995 example)
strategies.construction: Borrow SGD at 3%, place INR NRNR deposit at 20%, hedge FX with a 3-year forward costing ~2%/yr
strategies.numbers: gross spread 17%; net ~15% riskless; 10 lakh -> ~17.5 lakh over 3 years
strategies.best_regime: large interest-rate differentials with hedged currency risk
strategies.adjustments: roll forward hedge; watch repatriation rules
strategies.risks: counterparty/country risk; hedge cost creep

quotes: Buy where it is cheap, sell where it is dear, at the same time - the difference is your profit, with no risk

summary: November's FII inflow topped Rs 60,000 crore - highest-ever monthly; FII futures at 82% long flags month-end correction risk historically; support 12,800 / resistance ~13,200; RBI policy seen status-quo on high inflation; expects pause, not collapse.
lessons: Extreme crowd positioning (75%+ long) is itself the risk - the correction historically arrives by month-end.
After record inflows, 'most positives already priced' justifies pausing, not panicking; support maps from tested levels.

summary: Margin anatomy via a live Zerodha calculator: ACC long/short costs the same ~1.76 lakh (span 146,940 + exposure 29,000) against 8.5 lakh notional; stock-future margins vary with volatility (ACC ~21%, Adani Ent 47%, Ashok Leyland 35%); exposure margin fixed at 2% index / 3.5% stock; long/short terminology, MTM, squaring up, physical delivery.
lessons: Both long and short sides post margin to the exchange - it is a default fund, not a payment
SPAN (Standard Portfolio Analysis of Risk) scales with volatility; exposure margin is a fixed add-on (2% index, 3.5% stock futures)
Squaring up (counter-trade) before expiry removes any delivery obligation; most futures trades are speculative and never delivered
Volatile stocks demand much higher margins (47% vs 21%) - position size must respect the margin, not the notional
quotes: In futures you never buy or sell - you go long or short; both sides pay margin to the exchange

summary: IPO vs OFS explainer: IPO money goes to the company; OFS is an existing shareholder (Government) selling. Walks through applying via a broker's online console (corporate actions > OFS > cutoff price for retail <2 lakh). IRCTC context: 2019 IPO at 320, rallied ~600% to ~2,000, OFS floor 1,367.
lessons: In an OFS the company gets nothing - an existing shareholder is exiting, so the process and risks differ from an IPO.
Retail applicants (<2 lakh) should bid at cutoff price to avoid being priced out.
A hot prior IPO listing does not guarantee OFS profits - IRCTC had corrected ~15% into the OFS.
quotes: An OFS is one shareholder offering his shares for sale - the company does not receive the money.

summary: Explains open interest from the seller's perspective: max-OI put = support and max-OI call = resistance because option SELLERS put up large margin (~1.2 lakh/lot vs a buyer's few thousand) and carry unlimited risk, so the market weights their conviction. Warns max-OI strikes migrate intramonth as sellers adjust.
lessons: Max-OI put strike is support only because sellers - who risk unlimited loss and post big margin - are concentrated there.
OI is contracts on both sides: every lot has a bear (buyer) and a bull (seller); analysts trust the seller's wallet.
Max-OI support/resistance is dynamic: after a 200-400 point fall, sellers shift OI to lower strikes.
Old vs new NSE sites differ only in shares-vs-contracts units (contract multiplier), not in data.
quotes: Options is a game where there is no level playing field - the buyer risks a few thousand, the seller risks lakhs with unlimited downside.

summary: Pre-launch explainer for Nifty Financial Services derivatives (launched 11 Jan 2021): 20 banks/insurers/NBFCs; beta 1.2 between Nifty (1.0) and Bank Nifty (1.36); 94% correlation to Nifty, 98% to Bank Nifty; contract size 40 (~5.5-6 lakh notional), 3 monthly + 7 weekly contracts, expiry last Thursday, strike interval 100, freeze qty 5,001.
lessons: Sector index design: FinNifty was built as the middle risk point between Nifty and Bank Nifty.
Contract size sets the margin ticket - a smaller notional index lowers the entry barrier.
Correlation stats (94%/98%) tell you a new index is not true diversification within the same family.
FII flows concentrated in financials (35% of holdings, ~48% of incremental flows) justified a financials index.

summary: Standard PCR (total put OI / total call OI = 1.81) screams crash territory (>1.7 historically preceded crashes; <0.8 marked bottoms). But far strikes pollute the ratio: he recomputes using only strikes within the month's plausible range (12,800-14,200): put OI 1.67 cr vs call 1.49 cr = PCR 1.12 - mildly bullish, no crash signal.
lessons: Raw PCR is distorted by far-OTM strikes nobody expects to trade - filter to the plausible monthly range.
Rule of thumb: PCR >1.7 = crash risk, PCR <0.8 = bottoming zone; between them, no signal.
Range width for filtering: about 1,000 points at month start, 700-800 by mid-month.
A filtered PCR of ~1.1-1.2 reads as mildly bullish, not bearish.

strategies.name: Range-filtered PCR
strategies.construction: Sum put OI and call OI only for strikes within expected monthly range (spot +/-1,000 early in month, +/-700-800 mid-month); PCR = put OI / call OI
strategies.numbers: Dec 2020: raw PCR 1.81 vs filtered 1.12 (put 1.67 cr, call 1.49 cr in 12,800-14,200)
strategies.best_regime: Weekly/mid-month sentiment read before taking directional or option-selling positions
strategies.adjustments: Recompute as the expected range narrows through the month
strategies.risks: Range guess can be wrong in trending/volatile months; still an OI-based sentiment proxy, not a timing signal

quotes: Why include a 15,000 call or a 5,000 put in the ratio when the market will never get there this month?

summary: V-recovery: Nifty 13,200→13,620 and Bank Nifty 29,000→30,000 in one session as Brexit deal and France-UK port news lifted Europe. Sold 13,000 PEs with conviction through the fall. IT stocks at ATHs on Accenture read-through; Reliance alone could add ~500 Nifty points reclaiming 2,400.
lessons: Conviction, not just knowledge or technicals, is what makes money through drawdowns.
Bull-market profit-booking is frequent because so many ride profits - corrections are structural.
